```{r}
#| echo: False
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
```

# Retrieve and load the  raw dataset into one location

```{r}
# Folder for raw data
raw_dir <- "../data/_raw"

# Dataset information
data_file <- "GSE162746_Raw_counts_collected.csv.gz"
data_path <- file.path(raw_dir, data_file)

data_url <- paste0(
  "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/",
  "GSE162nnn/GSE162746/suppl/",
  data_file
)

# Create folder if it does not exist
if (!dir.exists(raw_dir)) {
  dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

# Download dataset if it is not already present
if (!file.exists(data_path)) {
  download.file(
    url = data_url,
    destfile = data_path,
    mode = "wb"
  )
}

# Check that the file exists
file.exists(data_path)

```
```{r}
#| echo: False
raw_data <- read_delim(
  data_path,
  delim = ";",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)
```

```{r}
dim(raw_data)
head(raw_data[, 1:5])
```

### Description of data variables:

Sequencing identifier associated with the sequencing samples. They look like sequencing run and barcode information Time (4h and 24h) Stimulation (Candita/ Aspergillus / Rhizopus / RPMI(control group)) Samples (8 samples that represent 8 biological replicates/ 8 different human donours) Gene expression data (The nymbers represent the number of sequencing reads assigned to each gene in each sample)

# Tidy the datasets:

### Metadata

```{r}

# Extract metadata directly from the first three rows
metadata <- as.data.frame(raw_data[1:3, ])

# Rename the first column
names(metadata)[1] <- "parameter"

# Convert the three metadata rows into columns
metadata <- as.data.frame(t(metadata[-1]))
colnames(metadata) <- as.character(raw_data[[1]][1:3])

# Add sample IDs as a column
metadata <- tibble::rownames_to_column(metadata, "sample_id")

# Rename columns
names(metadata)[names(metadata) == "sample"] <- "donor"
names(metadata)[names(metadata) == "stimu"] <- "stimulus"

# Recode stimulus names
metadata <- metadata |>
  mutate(
    stimulus = recode(
      stimulus,
      "RPMI" = "Control_group",
      "Candida-albicans" = "C_albicans",
      "Aspergillus-fumigatus" = "A_fumigatus",
      "Rhizopus-oryzae" = "R_oryzae"
    ),
    time = factor(time, levels = c("4h", "24h"))
  )

head(metadata)
```

```{r}
dim(metadata)
summary(metadata)
```
### Gene counts:

```{r}
gene_counts <- as.data.frame(raw_data)
names(gene_counts)[1] <- "gene_id"

gene_counts <- gene_counts |>
  filter(str_starts(gene_id, "ENSG"))
```

```{r}
dim(gene_counts)
head(gene_counts[, 1:5])
```

```{r}
#Any missing value?
metadata |>
  summarise(
    missing_sample_id = sum(is.na(sample_id)),
    missing_time = sum(is.na(time)),
    missing_stimulus = sum(is.na(stimulus)),
    missing_donor = sum(is.na(donor))
  )

gene_counts |>
  summarise(
    missing_gene_id = sum(is.na(gene_id)),
    missing_values = sum(is.na(as.matrix(select(gene_counts, -gene_id))))
  )
```

# Analysis of Candida albicans versus control group``

## From the two main datatables pulling only the data necesery for analysis:

#Table 1

1.  Filter the metadata based on fungi and control group

```{r}
metadata_candida_4h <- metadata |>
  filter(
    time == "4h",
    stimulus %in% c("C_albicans", "Control_group")
  )

```

#Table 2

1.  Extract sample ID's for C_albicans and Control group

```{r}
sample_ids <- metadata_candida_4h$sample_id
```

2.  Filter the count matrix with the extracted values by columns

```{r}
gene_counts_candida_4h <- gene_counts |>
  select(gene_id, all_of(sample_ids))


```

## Inspecting the data:

We have two tables with given dimensions.

```{r}
#check amount of rows and columns
dim(metadata_candida_4h)
dim(gene_counts_candida_4h)
```
```{r}
#make sure gene counts are numeric:
gene_counts_candida_4h <- gene_counts_candida_4h |>
  mutate(
    across(-gene_id, as.numeric)
  )
#check
sum(is.na(gene_counts_candida_4h[-1]))
```

```{r}
summary(gene_counts_candida_4h[, -1])
```
Many zeros: The median is 0 in every sample. At least half of the genes have zero counts.

Strongly right-skewed counts: The means are much higher than the medians.

Large differences between genes: Some genes have very high counts, with maximum values above 200,000 in some samples.

We have 32 observations - samples in metadata, 8 for each donor (A to H) for fungi(8) and control(8), at two different time points (4h and 24h) each sample has corresponding 61892 reads of different gene expression withing that sample in the gene counts table.

### Check sequencing depth (calculating total counts per sample):

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

library_sizes <- gene_counts_candida_4h |>
  summarise(
    across(-gene_id, sum)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "sample_id",
    values_to = "total_counts"
  )

library_sizes
```

### Visualising diference:

```{r}
ggplot(library_sizes, aes(x = reorder(sample_id, total_counts),
                          y = total_counts)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Sequencing depth per sample (4h)",
    x = "Sample",
    y = "Total raw counts"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
Why this matters: We need to account for sequencing depth before comparing Candida albicans with the control group.


### Comparing sequencing depth:

```{r}
library_sizes |>
  left_join(metadata_candida_4h, by = "sample_id") |>
  group_by(stimulus) |>
  summarise(
    mean_counts = mean(total_counts),
    median_counts = median(total_counts),
    min_counts = min(total_counts),
    max_counts = max(total_counts)
  )
```
The control group has a higher average sequencing depth. Therefore, comparing raw counts directly could be misleading.

### Preparing the sample information and sequencing-depth offsets.

```{r}
sample_info <- metadata_candida_4h |>
  left_join(library_sizes, by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(
    stimulus = relevel(factor(stimulus), ref = "Control_group"),
    donor = factor(donor)
  )
```
```{r}
head(sample_info)
```

### Using quasi-Poisson generalized linear model (GLM) using purr















works with raw counts and acounts for:
Sequencing depth through a library-size offset.
Donor differences through donor.
The treatment effect through stimulus

```{r}
# Select the first gene
gene_id_test <- gene_counts_candida_4h$gene_id[1]

# Extract its raw counts in the same sample order as sample_info
gene_counts_test <- as.numeric(
  unlist(
    gene_counts_candida_4h[1, sample_info$sample_id],
    use.names = FALSE
  )
)

# Prepare the data
test_data <- sample_info |>
  mutate(count = gene_counts_test)

# Fit the quasi-Poisson model
model_test <- glm(
  count ~ donor + stimulus + offset(log(total_counts)),
  family = quasipoisson(link = "log"),
  data = test_data
)

summary(model_test)
```
```{r}
gene_results <- lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(gene_counts_candida_4h)),
  function(i) {

    gene_counts <- as.numeric(
      unlist(
        gene_counts_candida_4h[i, sample_info$sample_id],
        use.names = FALSE
      )
    )

    test_data <- sample_info |>
      mutate(count = gene_counts)

    model <- glm(
      count ~ donor + stimulus + offset(log(total_counts)),
      family = quasipoisson(link = "log"),
      data = test_data
    )

    coefficients <- summary(model)$coefficients

    data.frame(
      gene_id = gene_counts_candida_4h$gene_id[i],
      log2FC = coefficients["stimulusC_albicans", "Estimate"] / log(2),
      p_value = coefficients["stimulusC_albicans", "Pr(>|t|)"]
    )
  }
)

gene_results <- bind_rows(gene_results) |>
  mutate(
    adjusted_p_value = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    significant = abs(log2FC) > 1 & adjusted_p_value < 0.05
  )
```

```{r}
dim(gene_results)
```

```{r}
head(gene_results)
```

```{r}
table(gene_results$significant, useNA = "ifany")
```
```{r}
gene_results |>
  summarise(
    upregulated = sum(
      log2FC > 1 & adjusted_p_value < 0.05,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    downregulated = sum(
      log2FC < -1 & adjusted_p_value < 0.05,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    total = sum(significant, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```


### Rerun on filtered genes:

```{r}
gene_results_filtered <- lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(gene_counts_filtered)),
  function(i) {
    gene_counts <- as.numeric(
      unlist(
        gene_counts_filtered[i, sample_info$sample_id],
        use.names = FALSE
      )
    )

    test_data <- sample_info |>
      mutate(count = gene_counts)

    model <- glm(
      count ~ donor + stimulus + offset(log(total_counts)),
      family = quasipoisson(link = "log"),
      data = test_data
    )

    coefficients <- summary(model)$coefficients

    data.frame(
      gene_id = gene_counts_filtered$gene_id[i],
      log2FC = coefficients["stimulusC_albicans", "Estimate"] / log(2),
      p_value = coefficients["stimulusC_albicans", "Pr(>|t|)"]
    )
  }
)

gene_results_filtered <- gene_results_filtered |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(
    adjusted_p_value = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    significant = abs(log2FC) > 1 & adjusted_p_value < 0.05
  )
```

```{r}
dim(gene_results_filtered)

table(gene_results_filtered$significant, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r}
gene_results_filtered |>
  summarise(
    upregulated = sum(
      log2FC > 1 & adjusted_p_value < 0.05,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    downregulated = sum(
      log2FC < -1 & adjusted_p_value < 0.05,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    total = sum(significant, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```


#VULCANO PLOT 4 H



```{r}
ggplot(gene_results_filtered,
       aes(x = log2FC, y = -log10(adjusted_p_value),
           color = regulation)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Upregulated" = "red",
    "Downregulated" = "blue",
    "Not significant" = "grey"
  )) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Volcano plot: C. albicans vs Control (4h)",
    x = "log2 Fold Change",
    y = "-log10 Adjusted p-value",
    color = "Regulation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
